# Demo 16: Marketplace — Asset Exchange

## Headline

Add a **Marketplace** module that lets ToneForge users **search, install and
publish procedural asset packages** — recipes, stacks, sequences and palettes —
distributed as versioned, license-declared, Validator-gated bundles rather than
static audio. Installing a package registers its assets into the local registry
so `toneforge generate` / `toneforge stack render` work immediately, and a
single install yields infinite deterministic variation at its original quality.

## Problem statement

ToneForge can generate, analyse, store, mix and (after Demo 12) compile assets,
but there is **no distribution layer**: creators cannot share the procedural
systems they build, and consumers must rebuild equivalent recipes by hand.
Without an exchange layer there is also no enforced point for quality,
licensing or provenance — broken or unlicensed assets can be copied ad hoc with
no gate. `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` specifies the exchange layer (procedural
assets only, Validator-gated, versioned, license-declared, fully inspectable),
and `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` §Demo 16 defines the demo narrative; this epic
delivers that slice end-to-end and measurably.

## Users

- **Sound designers / producers** who publish reusable asset packs and want
  their work discoverable and safely reusable.
- **Technical artists / gameplay engineers** who acquire packs and need them to
  integrate into the project registry immediately and behave deterministically.
- **Teams / studios** running private registries or offline mirrors with
  controlled licensing and versioning.
- **Maintainers** who need a hard quality gate so invalid assets never reach the
  marketplace or the local library.

Example user stories:

- As a sound designer, I want to publish a validated package (name + semver)
  so others can reuse my recipes and stacks without me shipping audio.
- As a gameplay engineer, I want to search a category, install
  `industrial_lasers@2.1.0`, and immediately run
  `toneforge generate --recipe il-heavy-cannon --seed 42` with byte-identical
  output across seeds.
- As a team lead, I want version conflicts (incompatible majors, already
  installed versions, missing/circular dependencies) detected and reported, so
  a dependency bump cannot silently break builds.
- As a maintainer, I want publishing to run the Validator, so no broken or
  invalid asset can be uploaded.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Search.** `toneforge marketplace search --category <c>` returns listings
   with metadata: `name@version`, author, contained asset counts (recipes,
   stacks, sequences, palettes), rating and license. Results are deterministic
   for identical registry state and support `--json`.
2. **Install.** `toneforge marketplace install <package>@<version>` fetches and
   verifies the package, validates it, registers its recipes/stacks/sequences/
   palettes into the local registry, and records provenance + the locked
   version. Installed assets work immediately: the installed recipe renders via
   `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>` and installed stacks render via
   `toneforge stack render`.
3. **Publish.** `toneforge marketplace publish --package <dir> --name <n>
   --version <v>` validates the package (manifest/schema, dependency
   resolution, determinism checks, license declaration and the Demo 12
   Validator) and **rejects** invalid packages with structured errors. Only
   passing packages are published, and published versions are immutable.
4. **Determinism & versioning.** Installed assets maintain determinism (same
   seed ⇒ byte-identical output, identical to a locally authored equivalent)
   and survive re-install reproducibly. Semantic versioning is enforced and
   version conflicts are detected and reported with actionable errors.
5. **Automated validation.** A deterministic conformance harness over a fixture
   registry/packages (no live network) covers search, install, publish,
   version-conflict detection and post-install determinism; unit + CLI
   integration tests cover the three commands and their `--json` contracts.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. Every child work item of this epic reaches a terminal stage (`in_review` or
   `completed`), and the epic is advanced to `in_review` only once all children
   are terminal and blockers are resolved.

## Constraints

- **Hard prerequisites.** Demo 12 Compiler & Validator
  (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate used by publish/install;
  Demo 15 Network & Integrations (`TF-0MLXFBHHW1BBO1ZJ`) supplies the transport
  and engine-adapter conventions the registry reuses. This work cannot begin
  until both land — which is why this item is **dependency-blocked**
  (`wl dep list TF-0MLXFBLNF1MCYS6Y`).
- **Procedural only, no executables.** Packages are textual, structured,
  regenerable assets — no binaries, no executable code, no runtime mutation
  (`MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §5, §13).
- **Validator-gated.** Invalid assets cannot be published or imported
  (`MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §7); the gate reuses Demo 12 rather than re-implementing
  it.
- **Semantic versioning & immutability.** Published versions are immutable;
  updates require a new version; updates are opt-in, never forced
  (`MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §5, §9, §11).
- **License & provenance.** Every package declares an explicit license and
  attribution; dependency license compatibility is checked
  (`MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §6).
- **Offline-testable.** Tests must not depend on a live network; the registry
  transport is abstracted behind an injectable interface with a local
  implementation (see Assumption A1).
- **Repository conventions.** New CLI command module in `src/cli/commands/`
  registered via `src/cli.yargs.ts`; declarative project config under
  `.toneforge/`; injectable-store precedence (`src/library/index-store.ts`,
  `SessionStore`); TypeScript strict (`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`) and
  the `vitest` suite stay green.

## Existing state

- No `src/marketplace/` module and no `marketplace` CLI command group exist
  (verified: no `marketplace` matches under `src/`; `src/cli.yargs.ts` registers
  no marketplace command).
- Neither prerequisite module exists yet: no `src/compiler`, `src/validator`
  (Demo 12, `in-progress` at `plan_complete`) and no `src/network`,
  `src/integrations` (Demo 15, `blocked` at `idea`).
- Building blocks that already exist and will be reused:
  - `src/library/` — `.toneforge-library/index.json` index store + storage,
    search and similarity (`src/library/index-store.ts`, `storage.ts`,
    `search.ts`, `types.ts`).
  - `src/core/recipe.ts` — `RecipeRegistry` and external recipe discovery
    (`discoverFileBackedRecipes`, `resolveExternalRecipeDirectory`).
  - `src/recipes/index.ts` — the built-in registry instance.
  - CLI command-module pattern (`src/cli/commands/library.ts`) registered in
    `src/cli.yargs.ts`.
  - `.toneforge/` project-local config directory (currently `mixer/`).
- `package.json` currently has no semver, archive or HTTP dependency; any new
  runtime dependency must be justified.
- `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` is authoritative; `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`
  §Demo 16 gives the canonical CLI sketch and proof points.

## Desired change

- New **`src/marketplace/`** module:
  - package **manifest** types + schema validation (name, version, type,
    dependencies, license, author, contained assets);
  - a **registry abstraction** (interface + local implementation) with search;
  - **install**: fetch → integrity check → validate → register assets into the
    local registry/library → lock version + record provenance;
  - **publish**: validate → reject-on-failure → immutable publish;
  - **semver/dependency resolution** with conflict detection and actionable
    errors.
- New **`marketplace`** CLI command group (`search`, `install`, `publish`)
  registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts`.
- Integration with the Demo 12 Validator and the existing library/recipe
  registry (no duplication of either).
- Deterministic fixture-based conformance tests plus unit and CLI integration
  tests.
- Documentation: README, a marketplace guide under `docs/guides/`, CLI help and
  cross-references to `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/marketplace/types.ts` — New: package manifest, listing, license and
  provenance types.
- `src/marketplace/manifest.ts` — New: manifest parsing + schema validation.
- `src/marketplace/registry.ts` — New: registry interface and the local
  (offline) implementation used by search/install/publish.
- `src/marketplace/search.ts` — New: deterministic, metadata-rich category
  search.
- `src/marketplace/install.ts` — New: fetch, verify, validate, register into the
  local registry, version-lock and provenance record.
- `src/marketplace/publish.ts` — New: validate (including the Demo 12 Validator)
  and immutable publish; structured rejection errors.
- `src/marketplace/version.ts` — New: semver compatibility and conflict
  detection (missing/circular dependencies, incompatible majors).
- `src/marketplace/index.ts` — New: public module surface.
- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts` — New: `search --category`,
  `install <package>@<version>`, `publish --package --name --version`
  (`--json`).
- `src/cli.yargs.ts` — Register the `marketplace` command group.
- `src/library/*` and `src/core/recipe.ts` — Register installed assets via the
  existing index store / registry (extend, do not fork).
- `src/compiler/*` / `src/validator/*` — Demo 12 module; the publish/install
  gate delegates to it.
- `src/test-utils/fixtures/` — New fixture registry + valid/invalid packages for
  conformance tests.
- `.toneforge/marketplace/` — New: local registry state / cache (created on
  demand; documented as local state and git-ignored if appropriate).
- `README.md`, `docs/guides/marketplace.md`, `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` —
  user-facing docs and cross-references.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: scope creep into Compiler/Validator/Network.** Demo 16 must reuse, not
  re-implement, Demo 12 and Demo 15. *Mitigation:* treat the Validator and
  transport as dependencies behind interfaces; record any new capability as a
  separate work item.
- **Risk: live-network dependence makes tests flaky.** *Mitigation:* abstract the
  registry transport and test against a local fixture registry; no live network
  in unit/integration tests.
- **Risk: non-deterministic installs** (asset ordering, cache races).
  *Mitigation:* deterministic ordering and content-addressed integrity checks;
  tests assert byte-identical output pre/post install.
- **Risk: silent version incompatibility.** *Mitigation:* enforce semver,
  detect conflicts (missing/circular/incompatible) and fail with structured,
  actionable errors; version-lock installs.
- **Risk: license/provenance drift.** *Mitigation:* require an explicit license
  and attribution in the manifest; validate dependency license compatibility;
  record provenance on install.
- **Risk: package format ambiguity** could cause rework. *Mitigation:* keep the
  manifest declarative and versioned; reconcile the exact on-disk layout during
  planning (Assumption A1).
- **Assumption A1:** the demo marketplace is backed by a **local/offline
  registry adapter** behind an injectable interface (a directory or local
  service), with a remote adapter delegating to Demo 15 Network. This matches
  `MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §12 (private registries / offline mirrors) and keeps the
  demo deterministic and testable without a public server. *For producer
  confirmation at plan time.*
- **Assumption A2:** packages are textual manifests plus structured assets
  (recipes/stacks/sequences/palettes); the archive/layout detail is a planning
  decision.
- **Assumption A3:** install registers assets into the existing `.toneforge-library/`
  index and recipe registry rather than a separate store.
- **Assumption A4:** this epic is decomposed by the plan skill; intake does not
  create children.

## Related work (manual)

- `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` — authoritative Marketplace specification
  (asset model, licensing, validation, versioning, determinism guarantees).
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` §Demo 16 — canonical demo narrative, CLI sketch and
  proof points.
- **TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD** "Demo 12: Compiler & Validator -- Production-Ready
  Assets" — hard prerequisite; supplies the Validator gate.
- **TF-0MLXFBHHW1BBO1ZJ** "Demo 15: Network & Integrations -- Distributed &
  Embedded" — hard prerequisite; supplies transport/registry and engine-adapter
  conventions.
- **TF-0MLXF8A901W1Y176** "Demo 7: Library -- Structured Asset Storage" —
  `.toneforge-library/` index/storage conventions reused by install.
- **TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W** "Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making" —
  upstream of Demo 12; supplied the CLI/JSON-contract patterns.
- **TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2** "Runtime Features" — parent epic; Demo sequencing and
  dependency order live here and in `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`.
- **TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1** "Demo 9: Runtime & State -- Real-Time Behavioral
  Sound" — common prerequisite of the demo chain.
- `docs/prd/COMPILER_PRD.md`, `docs/prd/VALIDATOR_PRD.md`,
  `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md`, `docs/prd/INTEGRATIONS_PRD.md` — specifications of
  the prerequisite modules this epic consumes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the seed context
(`docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` §Demo 16, `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` and the
parent epic's intake brief) was sufficient to draft this brief. The decisions
below were resolved from repository evidence and are recorded for auditability.

- **Q1 (registry backend).** How is the marketplace backed for a local,
  deterministic demo?
  - Options considered: (A) a live public service; (B) a local/offline registry
    adapter behind an injectable interface (remote adapter delegates to Demo 15);
    (C) filesystem-only with no abstraction.
  - **Answer (agent, resolved from repo evidence): B — recorded as Assumption
    A1.** Rationale: `MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §12 lists private registries and
    offline mirrors as supported access models; the repo's tests are offline and
    deterministic; and Demo 15 supplies the networking layer, so the transport
    must be abstracted to satisfy both. *Flagged for producer confirmation at
    plan time.*
  - Source: `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §10–§13; repo test conventions.

- **Q2 (package contents).** What may a package contain?
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** procedural, textual assets —
    recipes, stacks, sequences, palettes (and other structured definitions) —
    with an explicit license and attribution; no binaries or executable code.
  - Source: `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §4, §5, §13.

- **Q3 (quality gate).** Where does validation happen?
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** on **both** publish and install,
    delegating to the Demo 12 Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) plus manifest,
    dependency and determinism checks; invalid assets are rejected on both
    paths.
  - Source: `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` §7, §9, §10; `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`
    §Demo 16 proof points.

- **Q4 (prerequisite sequencing).** Can this work start now?
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence): no.** Demo 12 and Demo 15 are hard
    prerequisites; dependency edges already exist and the item is auto-blocked
    by `reconcileDependentStatus`. Intake may prepare this brief, but
    implementation must wait until both prerequisites complete.
  - Source: `wl dep list TF-0MLXFBLNF1MCYS6Y`; `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`
    §Demo 16 ("Prerequisite Demos: 12, 15").

## Related work (automated report)

- **TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2** – Runtime Features (open)

## Plan

Planning pass for Demo 16 (effort **Large**, risk **Medium**). The producer approved the
feature plan and selected the recommended options (Appendix Q5-Q7). **Authorised
deviation:** the producer authorised creating this decomposition while the item remains
dependency-blocked (Appendix Q8). The item could not be claimed — `wl update --status
in-progress` is auto-reverted to `blocked` by `reconcileDependentStatus` because its
active blockers remain — so the SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 claim guard could not be satisfied;
no status regression beyond that automatic re-block was applied. The item legitimately
rests at `blocked`/`plan_complete` until Demo 12 and Demo 15 complete.

**Phasing (test-first, vertical slices).** Each phase cuts through all layers
(types -> logic -> CLI/registration -> tests -> docs). Between phases, review and update
the next items' descriptions with what was learned.

1. **Phase 1 - tracer bullet (listing):** F1 harness + F2 manifest + F3 registry/search.
2. **Phase 2 - install:** F4 version/conflicts + F5 install + F8 registry integration.
3. **Phase 3 - publish + CLI:** F6 publish + F7 CLI.
4. **Phase 4 - docs:** F9.

**Children (test-first order)**

| Feature | Work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry | TF-0MUZX3XAI003S1GN | task | - |
| F2 Package manifest types and schema validation | TF-0MUZX3XLO006D7HW | feature | F1 |
| F3 Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search | TF-0MUZX3XWW008FO77 | feature | F1, F2 |
| F4 Semver and dependency conflict detection | TF-0MUZX3Y8R008IPVP | feature | F1, F2 |
| F5 Marketplace install pipeline | TF-0MUZX3YKC002LZYB | feature | F1, F2, F3, F4, Demo 12 |
| F6 Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate | TF-0MUZX3YVJ001VHLN | feature | F1, F2, F4, Demo 12 |
| F7 Marketplace CLI command group | TF-0MUZX3Z7F000NJLQ | feature | F3, F5, F6 |
| F8 Register installed assets into library and recipe registry | TF-0MUZX3ZIU008KIXL | feature | F5 |
| F9 Marketplace documentation | TF-0MUZX3ZU3008FQH3 | docs | F7 |

**Resolved decisions**

- **D1 (Assumption A1):** local/offline registry adapter behind an injectable interface;
  the remote adapter delegates to Demo 15 later (Appendix Q5).
- **D2 (package layout):** directory bundle `manifest.json` + `assets/` (recipes, stacks,
  sequences, palettes as JSON/YAML) with content-hash integrity — no new runtime
  dependency (Appendix Q6).
- **D3 (demo asset scope):** recipes, stacks, sequences and palettes only, with
  `manifest.type` extensible to the wider PRD Section 4 list later (Appendix Q7).

**Acceptance-criteria coverage (manual review).** Parent AC1 -> F3, F7; AC2 -> F5, F8, F7;
AC3 -> F6, F7; AC4 -> F4, F5; AC5 -> F1; AC6 -> F9; AC7 (full suite) -> all features;
AC8 (epic meta) -> epic itself. The automated `tree_coverage` review returned a vacuous
`proceed` (0 parent ACs) because the brief uses a numbered AC list while the shared helper
parses only `- ` bullets; the manual mapping above is authoritative for this epic.
Recorded as a known tooling limitation of `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`.

**Plan: changelog**

- 2026-10-08 - `plan` skill: decomposed into 9 test-first children (F1-F9); wired 17
  dependency edges (including Demo 12 for F5/F6); recorded Appendix Q5-Q8; advanced stage
  to `plan_complete` (status remains `blocked` on Demo 12 + Demo 15 by design).

## Appendix (plan-time clarifications)

Extends the intake Appendix above; the intake entries Q1-Q4 are unchanged.

- **Q5 (registry backend - confirms Assumption A1).** How is the marketplace backed for a
  local, deterministic demo?
  - Options: (A) local/offline registry adapter behind an injectable interface (remote
    adapter delegates to Demo 15); (B) a live/remote HTTP adapter required in this demo;
    (C) filesystem-only with no abstraction.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply at plan time): A.** Resolves Assumption A1.
    Rationale: offline-deterministic tests and PRD Section 12 private/offline registries.

- **Q6 (on-disk package layout).** Which package format do publish/install use?
  - Options: (A) directory bundle `manifest.json` + `assets/` with content-hash
    integrity, no new runtime dependency; (B) a single tar/zip archive adding an archive
    dependency.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply at plan time): A.**

- **Q7 (demo asset scope).** Which asset kinds does this demo support?
  - Options: (A) recipes, stacks, sequences and palettes only (matches the roadmap and
    epic AC2), extensible later via `manifest.type`; (B) the full PRD Section 4 list now.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply at plan time): A.**

- **Q8 (proceed while blocked).** The item is dependency-blocked on Demo 12 (in-progress)
  and Demo 15 (blocked) and cannot be claimed for planning.
  - Options: (A) defer planning until both prerequisites complete (the project's default
    practice); (B) explicitly authorise creating the feature decomposition while the item
    stays blocked.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply at plan time): B.** Rationale: the decomposition
    is derivable from `docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` and the Demo 16 roadmap narrative and
    lets the gated children be blocked precisely; this is a documented deviation from the
    project's default of deferring blocked children.

# Reporting script, used-sounds fixture, and end-to-end test

## Goal

Deliver the reusable core artefact of the machine-use demo: a standalone
`scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` batch script that consumes
`toneforge list recipes --category <c> --json`, removes recipes recorded in a
project's already-used-sounds list, and reports the remaining candidates —
human-readable by default, structured JSON with `--json`. Ship it with a
committed fixture and an end-to-end regression test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` exists and:
   (a) resolves the `toneforge` CLI, falling back to `npx --prefix <repo-root>` when not on `PATH`;
   (b) accepts a category (default `card-game`) and a used-sounds file path (default a committed fixture);
   (c) calls `toneforge list recipes --category <category> --json` and parses the `recipes` array with Node.js (`node -e`), adding no new runtime dependency;
   (d) filters out recipes whose `name` appears in the used-sounds file;
   (e) prints a human-readable summary by default (category, total, used, remaining, remaining names) and a structured JSON object when invoked with `--json`, containing at least `command`, `category`, `total`, `used`, `remaining`, `candidates`.
2. The script exits 0 on success, including when every category item is already used (empty candidate list), and exits non-zero with a clear diagnostic when the used-sounds file is missing/malformed or the CLI call fails.
3. A committed used-sounds fixture exists (e.g. `demos/fixtures/used-sounds.txt`) — a small newline-delimited sample used by both the demo and the test.
4. An automated test (e.g. `src/demo/machine-use.integration.test.ts`) spawns the script end-to-end against the fixture and a known category, asserting that used recipes are excluded, non-used recipes are included, and the `--json` report parses as valid JSON with the expected fields; it also asserts the empty-result path exits 0.
5. The script does not change CLI behaviour or existing human-readable CLI output.
6. `npm test` passes with the new test included.

## Key Files

- `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` — new reporting batch script.
- `demos/fixtures/used-sounds.txt` — new committed used-sounds fixture.
- `src/demo/machine-use.integration.test.ts` — new end-to-end test.
- `demos/demo-07-library.sh` — style precedent (CLI resolution + `node -e` JSON parsing).
- `scripts/generate-tableau-example.sh` — style precedent for a standalone `scripts/*.sh` batch script.
- `src/cli/commands/list.ts` — reference only; the `list recipes --json` contract consumed unchanged.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependency (`jq` may be mentioned as an optional extra, never required).
- Headless and deterministic.
- Follow existing `scripts/*.sh` style (`set -euo pipefail`, worked-example header comment, `TONEFORGE` resolution).

## Dependencies

None (first slice). The demo walkthrough (TF-0MUX1H0NF007GUSJ) depends on this item.

# Machine-use demo walkthrough (demos/machine-use.md)

## Goal

Author the user-facing walkthrough that motivates and demonstrates the
JSON-driven reporting workflow, driving the reporting script delivered by
TF-0MUX0XKCC0088GV4.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `demos/machine-use.md` exists with valid front matter (`title`, `id: machine-use`, `description`) and `##` step headings, following `demos/README.md`.
2. The walkthrough motivates the problem (choosing new placeholder sounds without reusing already-placed ones), shows raw `toneforge list recipes --category card-game --json` output, runs `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` (human-readable then `--json`), and shows the JSON report composing with further tooling (e.g. a generation queue), noting human output is unchanged.
3. Every executable `bash` code block uses `toneforge` as the command name and is runnable/headless.
4. The file parses cleanly with `src/demo/parser.ts` and satisfies the existing `src/demo/parser.integration.test.ts` constraints (valid front matter, ≥1 step, ≥1 toneforge command).
5. The walkthrough references the committed fixture and the reporting script paths accurately.

## Key Files

- `demos/machine-use.md` — new walkthrough.
- `demos/README.md` — convention reference; index update is a separate docs item.
- `demos/recipe-filtering.md` (Act 7) — narrative precedent for `list recipes --json`.
- `demos/batch-generation.md` — precedent for a batch-oriented walkthrough.
- `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` — the script the walkthrough drives.

## Dependencies

Blocked by TF-0MUX0XKCC0088GV4 (script + fixture + test).

# Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry

## Goal

Provide the deterministic, offline test foundation for the Marketplace slice so every
later feature is verified by a shared harness over fixture packages rather than a live
network.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic conformance harness runs with **no live network access** and fails
   if any marketplace test attempts one.
2. A fixture registry plus package fixtures cover: a valid publishable package, an
   invalid-manifest package, a version-conflict package, and a package with a missing
   dependency.
3. The harness asserts search listings, install registration, publish rejection,
   version-conflict detection and post-install determinism (same seed => byte-identical
   output).
4. The harness is wired into `npm test` and the full project test suite (`npm test`)
   passes with the marketplace changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/test-utils/fixtures/marketplace/` with a fixture registry directory and the
  valid/invalid package fixtures.
- Add fixture loader helpers mirroring existing `src/test-utils/` conventions.
- Add `src/marketplace/conformance.test.ts` (written first, initially failing) that
  exercises the five behaviours above through the marketplace public API.
- No live network; the fixture registry is the only backend used.

## Deliverables

- Fixture registry and package fixtures.
- Reusable fixture loader helpers.
- Conformance harness test file wired into the suite.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first foundation).
data.title: Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry

# Package manifest types and schema validation

## Goal

Define the declarative, versioned Marketplace package manifest and validate it
deterministically before any asset is published or installed
(`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 4, 5, 13).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A manifest schema covers `name`, `version` (semver), `type`, `dependencies`,
   `license`, `author`/attribution and the contained asset inventory.
2. `parseManifest` rejects missing or invalid fields (empty name, malformed semver,
   missing license) with structured errors that name the offending field.
3. Valid packages parse into typed manifests; parse -> validate is idempotent.
4. Unit tests cover valid, boundary and invalid cases and precede the implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/types.ts`: manifest, listing, license, provenance and error types.
- `src/marketplace/manifest.ts`: `parseManifest` / `validateManifest` returning typed
  results with structured error lists.
- `src/marketplace/manifest.test.ts`: tests written first.
- No new runtime dependency: validate the manifest shape in TypeScript.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/types.ts`
- `src/marketplace/manifest.ts`
- `src/marketplace/manifest.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Manifest types + parser/validator.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry) provides the fixtures.
data.title: Package manifest types and schema validation

# Semver and dependency conflict detection

## Goal

Enforce semantic versioning and detect version conflicts with actionable errors so a
dependency bump cannot silently break builds (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 5,
9, 11).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Semver parsing, comparison and range compatibility are implemented (or delegated to a
   vetted minimal implementation) without adding an unjustified runtime dependency.
2. Missing, circular and incompatible-major dependencies each produce a distinct,
   actionable structured error.
3. Resolution is deterministic and independent of input ordering.
4. Unit tests cover each conflict class and the compatible case and precede the
   implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`: semver helpers plus dependency resolution and conflict
  classification.
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`: tests written first, using F1 fixtures.
- Prefer a small in-repo implementation over a new dependency (`package.json` currently
  has no semver library).

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Semver + dependency resolution helpers.
- Structured conflict errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
data.title: Semver and dependency conflict detection

# Marketplace install pipeline

## Goal

Deliver `install(package@version)` end-to-end: fetch -> integrity check -> validate ->
register assets -> version lock + provenance (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7,
8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Install fetches from the registry, verifies content-hash integrity, validates the
   manifest and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages and integrity failures are rejected **before** any local
   registration occurs.
3. A successful install registers recipes/stacks/sequences/palettes, records provenance
   and locks the exact version.
4. Re-installing the same version is reproducible (identical registered state and
   byte-identical outputs).
5. Unit and integration tests use the fixture registry only (no live network).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`: orchestrate the pipeline against the F3 registry and F4
  resolver, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`: tests written first; failure paths before success.
- Registration into the library/recipe registry is completed by F8.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Install pipeline with integrity, validation, version lock and provenance.
- Unit + integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.
data.title: Marketplace install pipeline

# Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate

## Goal

Deliver `publish(packageDir, name, version)` that validates a package (including the
Demo 12 Validator), rejects invalid packages with structured errors, and publishes
immutably (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7, 9).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Publish validates manifest/schema, dependency resolution, determinism checks, license
   declaration and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages are rejected with structured errors and nothing is published.
3. Published versions are immutable; republishing an existing version fails with an
   actionable error.
4. Unit tests cover the reject and publish paths via the fixture registry.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`: validation orchestration + immutable write to the
  registry adapter, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`: tests written first; rejection paths before success.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Publish pipeline with Validator gate and immutability.
- Structured rejection errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.

# Marketplace CLI command group

## Goal

Expose the Marketplace through a `marketplace` command group registered in the yargs CLI,
with the documented `--json` contracts (`docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` Demo 16).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `toneforge marketplace search --category <c>` returns listings and supports `--json`.
2. `toneforge marketplace install <package>@<version>` installs and reports the
   registered assets, and supports `--json`.
3. `toneforge marketplace publish --package <dir> --name <n> --version <v>` validates
   and publishes, and supports `--json`.
4. The `marketplace` group is registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts` and appears in CLI help.
5. CLI integration tests cover all three commands and their `--json` contracts.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`: command module following the
  `src/cli/commands/library.ts` pattern.
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`: register the group.
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`: tests written first against the fixture
  registry.

## Key Files:

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Marketplace CLI group (search/install/publish) with `--json`.
- CLI integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).
- F6 (Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate).

# Register installed assets into library and recipe registry

## Goal

Make installed marketplace assets usable immediately by registering them through the
existing library index store and recipe registry rather than a forked store
(`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Installed recipes are available immediately via
   `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>`.
2. Installed stacks render via `toneforge stack render`.
3. Registration reuses the existing `src/library/` index store and
   `src/core/recipe.ts` registry (extend, do not fork), plus Demo 7 conventions where
   present.
4. An installed asset produces byte-identical output to an equivalent locally authored
   asset for the same seed.
5. Integration tests cover `generate` and `stack render` against a fixture install.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/library/index-store.ts` and `src/core/recipe.ts` registration helpers as
  needed.
- Wire registration from `src/marketplace/install.ts` into the existing registry.
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`: tests written first.

## Key Files:

- `src/library/index-store.ts`
- `src/core/recipe.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Installed assets registered into the local registry.
- Determinism integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).

## Goal

Wire received behavioural events into the Demo 9 runtime/state pipeline so that two
clients play deterministically identical audio, and demonstrate the bandwidth proof in a
two-window browser demo.

## What the user sees

Two browser windows side by side: the host changes state (`walk` -> `run`) and both windows
play deterministically identical audio; the network payload is behavioural events, not
audio.

## Minimal implementation

- Adapter from received behavioural events to the runtime/state API (reuse Demo 9;
  do not fork runtime logic).
- Two-window demo served by the existing web server (extend `web/server`).
- Bandwidth measurement surfaced in the demo/tests.
- Offline integration tests plus a documented manual demo.

## Key Files

- `src/network/runtime-bridge.ts` — New: event -> runtime/state execution.
- `src/runtime/runtime.ts`, `src/state/state.ts` — Reuse the Demo 9 pipeline (extend if needed).
- `web/server/index.ts` — Add a network demo WebSocket endpoint / host.
- `src/network/__tests__/runtime-bridge.test.ts` — New: integration tests.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 2, 6.4 (runtime integration).

## Constraints

- Reuse Demo 9 runtime/state; do not duplicate playback logic.
- Deterministic playback: the same event stream yields the same sound sequence.
- Keep the network payload under the 1 KB/s budget for the demo stream.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Received behavioural events execute through the Demo 9 runtime/state pipeline.
2. Two clients given the same event stream produce identical playback (same resolved
   sound sequence) - parent AC1.
3. A two-window browser demo served by the existing web server shows synchronised
   host -> client transitions.
4. Measured bandwidth for the demo stream is under 1 KB/s - parent AC2.
5. Offline integration tests plus a documented manual demo; full project test suite
   passes.

## Risky assumptions

- The Demo 9 runtime exposes an API that can execute a received event without side effects
  on local authority; if an adapter seam is missing, it is added minimally.
data.title: Network to Runtime/State integration and two-window demo

data.comment:
Implementation complete (pending finish gate).

## What was built

- src/network/runtime-bridge.ts — createRuntimeBridge(): receives canonical BehaviouralEvents and executes them through the Demo 9 runtime/state pipeline (reusing createRuntime/createStateMachine/createContext; no forked runtime logic). State changes transition the machine, context changes re-resolve recipes, discrete events re-fire the active sequence seeded by the event. Also measureStreamBandwidth() + canonicalEventByteSize() for AC2's 1 KB/s budget.
- src/network/__tests__/runtime-bridge.test.ts — 12 offline integration tests (execution, two-client determinism both directly and over an in-memory network session, bandwidth < 1 KB/s, lifecycle).
- web/server/network-relay.ts — host-authoritative /ws/network behavioural-event relay (transport only; no playback/runtime logic). Latest event is the late-join snapshot; relay stats expose bytes relayed.
- web/server/index.ts — wires /ws/network into the existing upgrade handler; exports networkRelay.
- web/src/network-demo.html + network-demo.ts — two-window demo: host controls broadcast state/surface events; every window resolves via the bridge, plays a deterministic ping, and shows a matching sequence fingerprint + live bandwidth.
- web/test/network-relay.test.ts — 4 integration tests for the relay (broadcast, authority, late-join snapshot, stats).
- docs/network.md (+ NETWORK_PRD §2/§6.4) — bridge semantics, bandwidth, and the documented manual two-window demo.

## Assumptions / decisions

- Bridge preserves the runtime's own seed for state/context-driven fires and uses the event's seed for discrete re-fires; determinism (identical resolved sequences across clients) is guaranteed and asserted.
- The web server relay is a dumb fan-out (host-authoritative); all sound resolution stays client-side through the bridge, so runtime logic is not duplicated. Chosen because web/server is a separate TS project (rootDir: server) that cannot import src/ without changing the build layout.
